entries.reason: FALSE POSITIVE via closure attribution, and the SAME artifact the sibling entry `ungated-vault-writer main.cmdCheck` records — reproduced here independently by a type-checked call graph, which is worth noting: two analyses with different anchor sets and different resolution models produce the same wrong answer for the same structural reason. The witness runs cmdCheck -> runCheck -> binaryInfo -> registeredToolCount -> tools.RegisterAll -> IngestCommitMsgTool -> [closure] -> atomicfile.Write. `vp check` COUNTS registered tools; it never invokes one. The derivation cannot tell registration from invocation because it deliberately attributes a closure's calls to the function that BUILDS it — without that edge no MCP handler is visible at all (see reachesSink). DECLARED WINS: the only vault write `vp check` performs is the transient, self-deleting .vp-fs-probe-*, and gating a diagnostic against a newer vault removes the tool an operator reaches for precisely when the surface mismatch is what they are diagnosing. Accepted.

🔴 THE LOAD-BEARING UNDER-DERIVATION, and the one that refutes generating the flag from the derived answer. Derived FALSE because `vp config sync` reaches no funnel primitive: internal/reconcile writes RAW — os.WriteFile/os.Remove/os.Rename at upgrade.go:80,84,88 and template_tree.go:502,510,555 — and the package contains no atomicfile or vaultfs call at all. The call graph is not lying; the funnel genuinely does not run there. DECLARED WINS: `vp config sync --prune` PRUNES what it writes, and adopting the derived answer would silently UNGATE it. That is a coverage regression of exactly the kind that sank the original move-the-gate thesis, and ADR-010's Consequence 'No coverage is lost — vp config sync --prune and vp audit vault --accept keep the gate they have today' is FALSE for a naive derivation on this half (it holds for vp audit vault --accept only because Phase 4 routed vaultaudit.Baseline.Save through atomicfile.Write). FIX DIRECTION, owned by the plan task's Phase 1: route internal/reconcile through the funnel, after which this entry goes STALE and must be deleted. Accepted until then.

DELIBERATE, and unlike the cmdCheck/cmdMCP entries the path is GENUINE: cmdHook -> runHook -> hook.Run -> archive.Create -> vaultfs.RenameNoLock is a real vault mutation reached by a real call chain. DELIBERATE, and the decision predates this rule. internal/mcp/tools.go: 'There is deliberately NO MCP startup gate — vp is MCP-primary, so the server stays up and the remediation surfaces in-band as a tool error payload.' Writes are gated PER TOOL at Registry.gateIfMutating, which both dispatch paths route through, and since 6254549 that gate is param-aware. A CLI-level mutates() here would refuse to start the server outright, taking vp_bootstrap_context away exactly when an agent needs to discover what is wrong. 🔴 GIT-MEDIATED — derived FALSE correctly, and gated anyway. `vp vault commit` mutates vault HISTORY exclusively through git, and the git channel is exempt from the write funnel BY VERB (a merge is N files in one operation, which no per-path primitive models; recorded on internal/sourceaudit/vault_write_funnel.go and re-ruled 2026-08-20). So it reaches no sink by the funnel's own definition, and a derivation that GENERATED the flag would silently ungate it. DECLARED WINS: git-mediated authorship is still authorship — `git merge` can leave conflict markers in resume.md — and a stale binary must refuse it. This entry, with its two siblings mcp.vp_vault_sync and mcp.vp_vault_tidy, is the reason the derivation pins rather than generates. Accepted, permanently: this one has no fix direction, because nothing here is broken.

🔴 FALSE POSITIVE FROM A SHARED GENERIC INSTANTIATION — an imprecision of VTA that neither ADR-010 nor the plan task anticipated, both of which worried only about CHA over-approximation. 🔴 GIT-MEDIATED — the sharpest instance of the ruling recorded on cli.cmdVaultCommit, because this tool sits on the recovery path. Derived FALSE: there is no funnel sink anywhere in internal/storage's vaultpull.go, vaultsync.go, vaultsyncflow.go or vaulttidy.go (verified by inspection and by this graph), so its vault writes are git's. DECLARED WINS — it commits and pushes vault history and a stale binary must refuse that. Adopting the derived answer would have LOOKED like a bonus, because the MCP-pull lockout ADR-010 records would dissolve on its own; it would have dissolved as a SIDE EFFECT while push and sync quietly lost their gate. The lockout was instead fixed deliberately in 6254549, by making the gate param-aware so action:'pull' passes while push and sync are still refused. Two ways to reach the same symptom, one of which also removes a gate: that is the whole argument for pinning rather than generating. Accepted, permanently.
